title: Graham Potter extends Sweden contract to 2030, two weeks before World Cup playoff
content:
Graham Potter has signed a contract extension as Sweden head coach, tying him to the job until 2030.

Potter was appointed on a short-term contract in October, weeks after his sacking by West Ham United, with the Swedish FA (SvFF) saying at the time that his deal would be automatically extended if Sweden qualified for the World Cup.

But two weeks before their World Cup qualifying play-off semi-final against Ukraine, Potter has extended his deal for four years in a significant show of faith from the SvFF.

Potter has overseen a 4-1 defeat to Switzerland and a 1-1 home draw with Slovenia in his two games in charge.

“I am incredibly happy about the continued collaboration with Graham Potter, who is a solid person whose leadership I appreciate and have strong faith in,” said Niclas Carlnen, secretary general of SvFF in a statement on Thursday.

“The long-term perspective gives players and managers peace of mind and the opportunity to create continuity in their activities with a view to future championships. Our national teams are of great importance to Swedish football and to many people around the country. Now we look forward to the coming years, but first and foremost, hopefully a World Cup summer.”

Kim Kallstrom, national team manager of the SvFF added: “Graham has already made a strong impression with his wonderful personality and professional attitude in his short time and we look forward to continuing our journey together.

“His coaching background is based on experiences from a wide and unique range, everything from Swedish football to high international level with the complexity that exists there. The fact that this is now clear gives us security for the upcoming playoffs.”

Potter said he felt “a great sense of pride and great responsibility” on extending his deal.

Sweden will face Ukraine in a one-0ff play-off game in Valencia, Spain on March 26, with the winner facing Poland or Albania for a place at this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

The 50-year-old former Brighton & Hove Albion and Chelsea boss was sacked by West Ham in September after winning only six games in his eight months in charge. He had taken charge of the club midway through the 2024-25 season.

Sweden finished bottom of their World Cup qualifying group but qualified for the playoffs on the basis of their Nations League performances.
